study_identification_part.si4_title: Individualized cerebellar damage predicts the presence of behavioral disorders in children with brainstem tumors

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Investigate cerebellar damage patterns resulting from pediatric brainstem tumors and their associations with behavioral disorders by building a normative model of cerebellar lobular volumes and evaluating prediction of behavior using total outlier count (tOC) and lobular volumes.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: Locally recruited children (Beijing); fcon_1000.projects dataset (IPCAS7); Child Connectome Project (CCNP); Children's Hospital Guangzhou
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The paper clearly states the four sources of healthy children data used to establish the normative model: 72 locally recruited children in Beijing (61 scanned), 69 from fcon_1000.projects dataset, 450 from Child Connectome Project (CCNP), and 269 from Children's Hospital in Guangzhou. After exclusions, 849 healthy children were included in the final analysis.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: To establish a normative model, data from 849 healthy children (age range: 4-18 years) were collected from publicly available databases, including 72 locally recruited children in Beijing (61 of whom underwent scanning), 69 from the fcon_1000.projects dataset (https://doi.org/10.15387/fcp_indi.corr.ipcas7), 450 from the Child Connectome Project (CCNP), and 269 from the Children's Hospital in Guangzhou.

rci2_hc_n.reason: The paper explicitly states that after excluding subjects with severe cerebellar compression or poor image quality, the final analysis included 849 healthy children.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: After excluding subjects with severe cerebellar compression or poor image quality, our final analysis included 147 patients and 849 healthy children.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Patients show widespread negative cerebellar deviations; higher tOC and reduced cerebellar volumes associate with greater social problems and withdrawal behaviors.
